church-of-the-east-under-the-mongols: Rabban Bar Sauma held row (yahballaha-sauma) is an anonymous Syriac abridgment of Sauma's own Persian account (Budge, line 779-783); not verbatim his words; Yahballaha III left out in all three rows because the same work is about him
rhineland-mysticism-and-the-friends-of-god: contested attribution: the Töss sister-book is "credited" to Elsbeth Stagel; her authorship is disputed
observant-reform-and-popular-preaching: Bernardino's Siena sermons are a listener's near-transcript (voices line)
joint: Humbert's 1054 excommunication (byzantine-imperial-church-macedonian, latin-papal-church-gregorian) is issued jointly by Humbert, Peter of Amalfi and Frederick
joint: Mar Jacob's quote (st-thomas-christians-1300-1517) is from the 1504 letter of four bishops (Yahballaha, Thomas, Jacob, Denha)
joint: Barsanuphius and John share one held row (chalcedonian-monasticism-judean-desert-and-gaza)

issued-in-name: Charlemagne's quote is from the Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae, a capitulary issued in his name (file creator: Anonymous); Theodoric's is a Variae letter drafted by Cassiodorus in his name; Huneric's is a royal edict

quoted-at-second-hand: these quotes reach the Library inside a later author's text or editor's note: Augustine of Canterbury (Bede), Radegund (Gregory of Tours), Columbanus (NPNF Gregory register), Huneric (Victor of Vita), Auxentius (inside Maximinus), Theodore Abu Qurrah (Newman's note, via Petavius), Bonaventure and Richard of St Victor (McCann's note), Joachim and Gerard of Borgo San Donnino (Denifle), Rainerius Sacconi (Racki), Nerses Shnorhali (Michael the Syrian, RHC), Gost Radin (Truhelka's transliteration of the testament)

attribution: Rainerius Sacconi quote is cited by Racki as 'Reiner op. cit.'; the edition is the Reinerius text in which the Summa de Catharis is embedded; moderate confidence it is Sacconi's Summa rather than the Passau Anonymous
attribution: Joachim quote is Denifle's excerpt from Joachim's writings, introduced by 'er' in Denifle's own German

recorded words: Olivi's quote is his declaration as recorded in the Spirituals' dossier (Ehrle III); Sawtrey's is his answer at examination as printed by Foxe; Dioscorus's and Tarasios's are synod minutes
OCR: several verbatim quotes keep OCR errors of the vendored files (coustat, luniinaria, Oklcastell, etemum, Île, Übertinus); they match the files exactly

person sort estimates: simeon-of-beth-arsham c.510 (before Severus 512); gregory-the-great 573 (before Leander 579); thomas-a-kempis 1399 (after Zerbolt 1394); john-wyclif 1372 (before Sawtrey 1400). If the person entries' start differs, re-check the order
Gregory the Great is a named voice in early-benedictine-italian-monasticism (held, Dialogues II) while his person entry is homed in roman-church-gregorian
rejected held: zara-yaqob row on the-ethiopian-monastic-flowering shelf is the royal chronicle about Zara Yaqob, not his own words; yahballaha-sauma rows rejected for Yahballaha III

not checked in depth (OCR too damaged or text not located): Heraclius's Ekthesis and Martin I's Lateran speeches in Mansi X; Zizka and Prokop letters in Palacky; Colette's letters; Ban Kulin's charter (not found in Miklosich)
